commit.message: Find Claude where the editor extension puts it (0.4.3)

findings.title: Lexicographic sort picks an older extension version as "newest"
findings.description: `entries.sort().reverse()` compares version suffixes as strings, so `anthropic.claude-code-1.9.0` sorts above `anthropic.claude-code-1.10.0`. On a machine with both left behind, the stale 1.9.0 binary is probed first and wins — the opposite of what the comment above promises, and the version-mismatch case this function was added to avoid.
findings.suggestion: Consider a numeric-aware comparison (`localeCompare` with `{ numeric: true }`) so 1.10.0 outranks 1.9.0. The same flaw exists in `versionManagerBins` above, which may be worth fixing in the same pass.

findings.title: Quadrupled worst-case discovery time: every candidate is probed twice at 60s each
findings.description: `anyRunnable` probes each candidate, then the main loop probes the same candidates again — results from the first pass are discarded. Raising the per-probe budget from 15s to 60s takes the pathological case (several existing-but-hanging candidates, e.g. a stalled antivirus scan) from 2×N×15s to 2×N×60s, and `checkStartup` is awaited during activation, so that time is blocked startup. Widening the candidate list with `editorExtensionBins` raises N on exactly the machines the change targets.
findings.suggestion: Consider having `anyRunnable` return the successful path (or record per-candidate results) so the main loop can reuse them rather than re-spawning, and/or capping total discovery with an overall deadline so no combination of candidates can stall activation for minutes.

findings.title: retryDetection can report a stale result when a start is already in flight
findings.description: `start()` returns immediately when the module-level `starting` guard is set (line 398), so if a recovery recheck or config-change restart is mid-flight, `await start(...)` does no work and the command then reports on whatever `session` happened to be from before. A user who just cleared the cache is told "still inactive" (or "active on …") based on the previous run, which is the exact ambiguity this command exists to remove.
findings.suggestion: Consider having `start` expose whether it actually ran (e.g. return a boolean, or await the in-flight promise), and in the command either wait for the running attempt or tell the user detection is already running.

findings.title: Comment says "ahead of everything else" but PATH still wins
findings.description: `locateClaude` pushes the override and the `fromPath()` hit into `candidates` before appending `candidatePaths()`, so the editor-bundled binary is only ahead of the other filesystem locations, not ahead of a `claude` on PATH. The comment's rationale (avoiding a version mismatch with what the editor runs) reads as if the ordering guaranteed something it does not.
findings.suggestion: Consider narrowing the comment to "ahead of the other install locations", or — if matching the editor's copy really is the priority — moving `editorExtensionBins` ahead of the `fromPath()` result in `locateClaude`.

findings.title: Module doc still claims a success is cached for the session
findings.description: The block comment on the `cached` declaration says "A success is cached for the session", which `SUCCESS_TTL_MS` now contradicts. Next reader has two adjacent comments disagreeing about the cache's lifetime.
findings.suggestion: Consider updating that sentence to mention the 10-minute expiry, or folding it into the new `SUCCESS_TTL_MS` docstring so there is one statement of the policy.

findings.title: Test fails confusingly instead of skipping when git isn't on PATH
findings.description: If no PATH entry matches `/git/i` with a git binary in it, `gitDir` is `undefined` and `process.env.PATH` becomes the empty string. `boot` then can't run git at all, the repo discovery goes dormant, and both checks fail with messages about the Claude CLI — pointing at the wrong subsystem. The `/git/i` heuristic also misses installs in directories not named "git" (e.g. `/usr/bin`).
findings.suggestion: Consider calling `skipped(...)` when `gitDir` is undefined, mirroring the existing `!real` branch, so an unfindable git is reported as a skip rather than a discovery failure. The stub `restore()` on line 316 could also move into the `finally` so a thrown check doesn't leak the stub.
